summary: Extends IMAP with an UNAUTHENTICATE command that lets an administrative client reuse one connection on behalf of several user identities. It avoids opening a new connection for each user.

eli5.summary: Instead of hanging up and redialing for every person, you tell the mail server to forget who you were and then act as someone new on the same call.

questions: reuse imap connection for multiple users
how to reuse an imap connection for multiple users
what does the unauthenticate command reset
is unauthenticate safe with imap proxies
subtitle: A new IMAP command that lets an administrative client switch users without hanging up and reconnecting.

tldr.problem: Trusted systems such as a voicemail gateway act for many IMAP users, but base IMAP forces them to close the connection and open a new one for each user.
tldr.mechanism: The UNAUTHENTICATE command resets all connection state except the TLS layer and returns the connection to the not authenticated state, so the client can authenticate again as someone else.
tldr.outcome: One connection, including its negotiated TLS session, can serve many identities. Servers must reset all per-user state carefully, and may not suit the most security-sensitive deployments.

today: RFC 8437 is a Proposed Standard from August 2018. It updates RFC 3501 and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why Reuse a Connection
sections.content:
Some IMAP deployments have peer systems with administrative privilege that act on behalf of end users. The RFC's example is a voicemail gateway that stores a user's voicemail over IMAP and marks it \Seen when the user listens to it by phone. Such a system can use the AUTHENTICATE command with administrative credentials to act for another user.

With the base specification, RFC 3501, the client must close the connection and make a new one for each user. For efficiency it is desirable to reuse the connection, particularly if SSL has been negotiated. This RFC adds the UNAUTHENTICATE command for that purpose, and it updates RFC 3501.
sections.eli5: Hanging up and redialing for every person is slow. This lets a helper stay on the line and just say who they are speaking for now.

sections.title: The UNAUTHENTICATE Command
sections.content:
The command takes no arguments and has no specific response. It directs the server to reset all connection state except for the state of the TLS layer, and the connection then returns to the not authenticated state. The result is OK when completed, or BAD if the command is unknown or the arguments are invalid.

If a mailbox was selected, it ceases to be selected, but no expunge event is generated. If a SASL security layer was active, the server ends its outgoing layer right after the CRLF following the OK, and the client ends its outgoing layer right after the CRLF following the command.

A BAD response only occurs if the command is issued in an invalid state, is not advertised, or breaks the syntax. A NO response is not permitted, so compliant implementations interoperate across the end of the security layer. A server that cannot reset its state MAY close the connection with an untagged BYE instead.
sections.eli5: You tell the server to wipe the whiteboard about who you are, but you keep the same private phone line. The server may only say yes or complain you asked wrongly.

sections.title: Re-authenticating and Discovering the Capability
sections.content:
After the command, the client may issue a new AUTHENTICATE or LOGIN as the server's capabilities allow. If no SASL security layer was active, the client is permitted to pipeline UNAUTHENTICATE with a following AUTHENTICATE. If the server also advertises SASL-IR (RFC 4959), an administrative client can re-authenticate in one round trip. This pipelining is the reason a server may not answer with NO.

Servers MAY advertise the UNAUTHENTICATE capability only after authentication has completed, so a client may need to issue CAPABILITY again after authenticating. The IMAP ID command (RFC 2971) is only for logs and audit files and has nothing to do with user identity, so how it interacts with UNAUTHENTICATE is left to the implementation.
sections.eli5: If there is no secret code in use, the helper can send the 'forget me' note and the 'I am someone new' note together in one envelope. Some servers only tell you they offer this after you have signed in.

sections.title: The Revised State Machine
sections.content:
The IMAP state machine in Section 3 of RFC 3501 has no path from the authenticated or selected state back to the not authenticated state. UNAUTHENTICATE adds one: transition 7 in the revised diagram.

The numbered transitions are: (1) connection with an OK greeting, (2) pre-authenticated connection with a PREAUTH greeting, (3) rejected connection with a BYE greeting, (4) successful LOGIN or AUTHENTICATE, (5) successful SELECT or EXAMINE, (6) CLOSE, UNSELECT or a failed SELECT/EXAMINE, (7) UNAUTHENTICATE, and (8) LOGOUT, server shutdown or connection closed.
sections.eli5: A mail connection moves through rooms: waiting at the door, signed in, looking at one mailbox, and leaving. This adds a hallway back to the door without leaving the building.

sections.title: Interactions With Other Extensions
sections.content:
Connection state for other IMAP extensions MUST be reset if both that extension and UNAUTHENTICATE are advertised and used. The rule applies to all current and future extensions except STARTTLS and ID. The RFC lists specific cases:

  • Cached identity information, such as group memberships used for access control lists (RFC 4314), MUST be reset.
  • CONDSTORE servers MUST behave as if no CONDSTORE-enabling command was issued.
  • If COMPRESS is active, the compression layer ends along with the SASL layer, compression first when it matters.
  • Anything turned on by ENABLE stops being enabled, including CONDSTORE, QRESYNC, METADATA, METADATA-SERVER and UTF8=ACCEPT.
  • With SEARCHRES, saved search results are discarded so $ is the empty set.
  • With LANGUAGE, the language reverts to i-default.
  • With CONTEXT=SEARCH or CONTEXT=SORT, there is an implicit CANCELUPDATE for all server contexts.
  • With NOTIFY (RFC 5465), notification state is cancelled and default behavior returns.
sections.eli5: Anything the last person switched on, like special settings or saved searches, gets switched off, so the next person starts fresh.

sections.title: Client Certificates and the imaps Port
sections.content:
A TLS client certificate does not normally affect the application layer, except when SASL EXTERNAL is used in AUTHENTICATE to authenticate as the IMAP user the certificate maps to. UNAUTHENTICATE breaks that application-level binding but does not discard the client credentials. An administrative client can therefore use one certificate with administrative privilege to act for many users on one connection via EXTERNAL.

Some servers on the imaps port use the certificate to authenticate at once as the certificate's default identity and signal this with a PREAUTH greeting (transition 2). Then certificates cannot be used for administrative proxy authentication unless UNAUTHENTICATE is also advertised. In that case the client answers the greeting with UNAUTHENTICATE and then issues AUTHENTICATE EXTERNAL.
sections.eli5: Your ID card for the building stays with you, but the server first treats you as whoever the card names. You can say 'forget that' and then pick who you are acting as.

sections.title: Security and Privacy Considerations
sections.content:
The original IMAP state machine allowed a design where each authentication identity matches an operating system identity and administrative privilege is revoked after login. This extension is not compatible with that approach. That approach has significant performance costs on Unix systems, so the extension suits environments where efficiency is a high priority, but may not be appropriate for the most security-sensitive ones.

Implementers must reset all server state so a later user inherits no data or privileges from the earlier one, including cached group membership, active notifications and per-user data such as flags.

Some IMAP proxies enter a pass-through mode after authentication. There, the command could let a client bypass restrictions present in the proxy but not in the backend. Servers MUST therefore provide a way to disable the extension. Mitigations are processing the command at the proxy layer, or enabling it only for administrative identities.

On privacy, the extension mostly changes nothing, though between data centers connection reuse could make traffic analysis harder.
sections.eli5: The risk is the next person accidentally keeping the last person's keys. So the server must clear everything, and the owner must be able to turn this feature off.
